title: finding(plugin-grid,plugin-view): both `explainDouble` helpers omit `record.visible` for a single-`recordId` request, so `useRecordEditable` fails open through them — against the helpers' own docblock, in the two files most likely to be copied
body:
Found by the `os-dev` lane delivering PR objectui#9809 (card objectui#7996) under that card's one-double fence, and **re-verified line by line by the reviewing seat** — which corrected one of its statements, see «What I corrected».

## What

Two shared test helpers answer `POST /api/v1/security/explain` for their package's suites:

- `packages/plugin-grid/src/__tests__/explainDouble.ts`
- `packages/plugin-view/src/__tests__/explainDouble.ts`

Read on `origin/main` (plugin-grid's copy; line numbers are its):

| line | reading |
|---|---|
| `:57` | `const recordIds = Array.isArray(body?.recordIds) ? (body!.recordIds as string[]) : undefined;` |
| `:62` | `allowed: true,` |
| `:67` | `...(recordIds ? { records: recordIds.map((id) => ({ recordId: id, visible: true })) } : {}),` |

⇒ the `records` array is spread **only** when the request carries `recordIds`. A request carrying a single `recordId` gets `allowed` / object / operation / principal / layers and **no `record.visible` member at all**.

## Why that is a contract violation rather than an omission

`packages/plugin-detail/src/useRecordEditable.ts` reads `decision?.record?.visible` and **returns early — fail open —** when it is not a boolean. So a single-`recordId` request through either helper takes exactly the path it would take on `ECONNREFUSED`.

⭐ And the helper's own docblock states the contract it breaks, at `:27`:

> The answer is `visible: true` for every id asked about, which reproduces the …

「every id asked about」 does not hold for an id asked about **singly**.

## Why it matters more than the card that found it

objectui#7996 repaired **one** inert double in one test file. These two are **shared helpers** — the files a reader reaches for when they need to answer this endpoint, and therefore the ones most likely to be copied. ⇒ the same defect class as objectui#7996, sitting in the highest-traffic position for it.

⚠️ **And the diagnosis objectui#7996 was filed under is imprecise, which is worth carrying here**: `allowed` is a **real** key of the explain response — `AccessExplainPanel.tsx:405`, `:410`, `:413` read `decision.allowed` for the OBJECT-level verdict (measured by the reviewing seat). So the failure is not a fabricated contract; it is **the wrong LAYER's shape handed to a ROW-level reader**. That is the sentence a future reader needs, because it also says when `allowed` is correct.

## ⚠️ What I corrected in the reporting lane's text

It calls plugin-view's file *"its per-package copy"*. **The two are not byte-identical** — md5 `2650630ec956f495e7a87e2fe599e0f2` (plugin-grid) against `3cd7e361f8bda009e79005b8f151f60d` (plugin-view). ⛔ I did **not** diff them, so what differs is unmeasured; whoever takes this reads both rather than assuming one patch applies twice. ⭐ Two copies of one helper that have already drifted is part of this card, not a footnote to it.

## ⛔ NOT MEASURED — and the taker needs this before acting

⛔ **Whether any consuming suite actually issues a single-`recordId` request through either helper.** The reporting lane names this as the gap and it is the one that decides whether this is live or latent. ⇒ take that reading first; if nothing issues a single-id request today, this is a trap for the next reader rather than a defect in a current run, and the fix is the same but the grading is not.

⛔ Whether the two helpers' divergence already changes their answers. ⛔ Whether other consumers besides `useRecordEditable` read the single-record shape. ⛔ About 20 other test files across packages carry an `allowed: true` fetch double — several are object-level permission doubles where `allowed` is the **right** key, so ⛔ that population is explicitly **not** part of this card and a sweep of it would be wrong.

Refs: objectui#7996 / PR objectui#9809 (the one-double repair that surfaced this, and the bound that kept it out) · objectui#7307 batch 1 (the landed example of the two shapes the hooks read) · `useRecordEditable.ts` and `useRecordCrudVerdicts.ts` (the two fail-open readers).
